pronunciation.approximation: Say "whiro" with the stress and length implied by the scholarly restoration "Whiro".
pronunciation.note: The ASCII form "whiro" is a DNS compromise; the restoration "Whiro" preserves the name's scholarly dignity.

domains.title: Whiro
domains.subtitle: Darkness
domains.lead: Whiro is darkness, evil. The name means "The lizard of death" and belongs to the polynesian tradition.

cards.name: Sacred Name
cards.desc: The restoration Whiro returns the figure to scholarly recognition.

cards.name: Living Tradition
cards.desc: Honored in polynesian myth, cult, and cultural memory.

symbols.meaning: The restored form Whiro, carrying scholarly and cultural weight.

mythology.lead: The stories of Whiro place darkness, evil at the center of a living mythological world.

myths.title: Origins
myths.text: Whiro appears in polynesian tradition as darkness, evil. The name's meaning, "The lizard of death", shapes the narratives told about this figure.

myths.title: Worship and Memory
myths.text: Devotees and later tradition-keepers preserved Whiro in ritual, text, and iconography, ensuring the name survived into the modern scholarly record.

lore.culturalLegacy: Whiro remains a touchstone for understanding polynesian religion, art, and identity.
